sources.story_title: NEWS TRIGGER — Commerce will “accept new proposals from states under the Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment program” targeting “newly identified unserved locations” made eligible by FCC map changes or program defaults. NTIA Administrator Roth visited Alaska for a roundtable with broadband providers; Sen. Dan Sullivan said the round could make “over 5,000” new locations eligible in his state.

CORROBORATION (in window) — NTIA describes the round as a “true-up” of eligible locations funded from “$21 billion in savings generated by the Commerce Department's Benefit of the Bargain reforms.” Roth announced it in Anchorage alongside Sen. Dan Sullivan and visited a planned BEAD site in Palmer. Policy notice issued 2026-09-03.

sources.outlet: U.S. Code (Office of the Law Revision Counsel)
sources.story_title: LAYER 1 PRIMARY — 47 U.S.C. 642. The Commission's statutory duty to build the broadband serviceable location fabric and identify unserved areas. This is the layer that manufactures “newly identified unserved locations.”

sources.outlet: U.S. Code (Office of the Law Revision Counsel)
sources.story_title: LAYER 2 PRIMARY + CHOKEPOINT — 47 U.S.C. 1702. The Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information (NTIA Administrator) approves or disapproves each state's final proposal and holds reallocation and deobligation authority over unspent funds, at 1702(c)(5)(C) and (g)(3). One statutory officer owns the approve / reject / reallocate binary.

sources.outlet: SEC EDGAR — GCI Liberty, Inc. Form 10-K (FY2025, filed 2026-02-11)
sources.story_title: LAYER 3 PRIMARY — GCI Holdings described as the leading integrated communication services provider in Alaska; rural construction explicitly conditioned on BEAD/IIJA subsidy availability. Note GCI was divested from Liberty Broadband on 2025-07-14, so GCI Liberty is the correct filer.

CONTEXT / basis for the derived savings estimate — Alaska's first-round BEAD approval of $629,172,951.83 across 29 projects and 15 providers (GCI $121.2M incl. AIRRAQ with Bethel Native Corporation; Alaska Communications $124M+). Against a >$1B Alaska allocation this implies roughly $370M+ unspent, which is why the post hedges that figure as an estimate rather than an agency number.

_access_notes: The NTIA Supplemental Deployment Policy Notice PDF itself could not be fetched this run (persistent HTTP 503 across every ntia.gov and broadbandusa.ntia.gov path, for both scouts and the mapper). fcc.gov, broadbandmap.fcc.gov and commerce.alaska.gov returned 403. Every layer was therefore re-anchored to a statute or filing that was actually fetched, rather than citing an unfetched page. Two provisional layers (Alaska Broadband Office re-bid, NIST grant-agreement final review) were dropped for lack of a fetchable primary source; dropping them does not break the FCC -> NTIA -> GCI chain or the chokepoint.
